About the Shop

A Fishermen's Eatery at the Edge of the Port

Marutoma Shokudo — with its sister shop Marumi Shoten — is a working port-market eatery in Tomakomai, on Hokkaido's Pacific coast. It is not a restaurant that buys seafood. It is a seafood shop that cooks: the same families who sort the morning landings run the counter, write the prices by hand, and decide what becomes today's bowl.

The doors open at 5:00 in the morning, when the port is already awake, and close at 2:00 in the afternoon — because by then, the best of the day is gone. Regulars are fishermen, market workers and travellers who plan their Hokkaido trips around breakfast here.

Tomakomai is famous across Japan for hokki surf clams and some of the richest uni in Hokkaido. At Marutoma, both go from shell to tray in sight of the harbour.

How Shipping Works

Port-Fresh, Frozen at the Source

The proposal: bring the counter's freshness to your door with a frozen cold chain that starts where the fish are landed — not at a warehouse.

01

Selected at the Counter

Your order is picked from the same morning-grade seafood sold at the shop — uni trays, crab and shellfish chosen by the people who priced them by hand.

02

Flash-Frozen & Packed at the Port

Items are prepared, vacuum-packed and frozen at the port in Tomakomai, locking in the texture and sweetness of the catch at its peak — no middlemen, no long storage.

03

Cold-Chain Delivery to Your Door

Orders travel in insulated frozen packaging with gel coolant, tracked door to door. Thaw in the refrigerator overnight and serve like sashimi — the way the counter intends.

Proposal note: shipping areas, fees and delivery schedules shown on this demo are a proposed service design for discussion with the shop — they are not yet a live service.

Good Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

Where can you ship to?

Under the proposal, frozen orders would ship throughout Japan first — including delivery to hotels for visitors — with selected international destinations (where frozen seafood imports are permitted) added step by step. Live items such as hokki clams would remain counter-only or domestic, so they arrive truly alive.

How fresh is frozen seafood, really?

Frozen at the port within hours of landing, seafood keeps the quality of the morning it was caught — often better than "fresh" fish that has spent days in transit. Uni and crab are portioned before freezing so nothing is refrozen or wasted, and every pack would carry its packing date.

How do I eat the uni and scallops?

Thaw slowly in the refrigerator (6–8 hours, or overnight). Serve uni as-is over warm rice with a little soy sauce and wasabi, or on its own by the spoonful. Scallops are sweetest raw as sashimi; a 10-second sear per side in a hot pan is the counter's other favourite. King crab legs just need a gentle steam or grill until heated through.

Why are some prices so low — ¥333?

That's the port talking. When a boat lands more than the market expected, Marutoma prices the surplus to move the same day — live hokki at ¥333 for two is a real post from the shop's Instagram. Sample prices on this demo come from those posts; live prices would follow the day's catch, just like the handwritten signs at the counter.

Can I visit the shop in person?

Yes — and you should. Marutoma Shokudo in Tomakomai opens at 5:00 AM and the best bowls sell out well before the 2:00 PM close. Follow @wasshoiiii_131 on Instagram for the day's arrivals and specials before you go.

Is this the shop's real online store?

Not yet. This page is a concept demo prepared as a proposal for the shop, to show what an English-language store could look like. Checkout is disabled and no orders or payments are taken.
